prompt:
A high-fidelity, photorealistic screenshot-quality rendering of a finished desktop website page, shown straight on, filling the frame edge to edge. No device frame, no browser chrome, no perspective, no drop shadow around the page. This is a finished production web page, not a wireframe and not a sketch.

Typography, used exactly: a warm high-contrast serif (in the manner of Newsreader) for the headline and all story prose; a clean geometric sans (in the manner of DM Sans) for labels, buttons and navigation; a monospaced face (in the manner of Fira Code) for the small uppercase labels and for anything shown as typed input.

Palette, used exactly: warm aged-paper off-white (#F7F3ED) as the main page background, dark warm ink (#2A231C) for text, muted slate blue (#365778) as the single accent used for buttons and emphasis, deep near-black warm brown (#171310) for dark blocks. No other hues. A very faint regular dot grid sits over the paper background.

The page is set in a wide centred column. Generous margins, generous line spacing, book-like reading measure for the prose. The overall character is a well-printed page: calm, editorial, made of paper and ink rather than of software. No cards with rounded corners, no drop shadows, no gradients, no glassy surfaces, no gloss, no icons, no illustrations of people, no logos other than the wordmark.

TREATMENT: with world imagery.

Same structure as a paper-based page, but each of the two world pairs in section one is introduced by its own wide, short, atmospheric image band running the full width of that pair, about one fifth the height of the page.

The first image band is a moody rain-slicked night street in a nineteen-forties port city, wet asphalt, a lit window, deep shadows, painterly and desaturated, tinted toward the page's warm ink and slate blue rather than full colour. The second image band is the interior of a small ship looking out through a forward port at empty dark space, sparse, quiet, the same restrained palette. Both images are painterly and grainy like a printed plate in a book, not photographic and not glossy, and both are muted enough that the text beside them stays dominant.

Beneath each image band sits that world's pair: the typed description on the left in monospace inside a deep near-black block, and the generated prose on the right in the serif on paper.

Section two has no imagery at all. It is centred on plain aged paper, and the absence of pictures after two image bands is what gives it weight. The three choice options are wide rectangles with thin dark borders in the serif, larger than the body prose, the chosen one with a slate blue left edge and slate blue text. The failed-check marker is in monospace, and the consequence passage follows with its first sentence in slate blue.

The closing band at the foot is a single wide rectangle on slightly warmer paper.

PAGE CONTENT. Render all of this text legibly and accurately. Spelling matters.

Header, small, top left: Narraitor
Header, small, top right, three items: About / Privacy / Terms

Headline, large serif: Play a story in any world you can imagine
Subhead, one line: You describe the world. It decides how the story sounds.
Primary button, filled: Start your story
Secondary text link beside it: How it works

SECTION ONE heading, small: YOU WROTE THIS. IT WROTE THAT.

Pair one.
Left, small label: YOUR WORLD
Left, in a monospaced face, as if typed: A rain-soaked port city where it never stops raining and every cop is on someone's payroll. Nineteen-forties, but the neon is wrong.
Right, small label: WHAT CAME BACK
Right, in a serif reading face: The rain had been going since Tuesday and showed no interest in stopping. Delacroix was waiting under the awning outside Kessler's, collar up, pretending to read a paper he had already read. He did not look up when I came alongside him. That was how I knew the money had already changed hands.

Pair two.
Left, small label: YOUR WORLD
Left, in a monospaced face, as if typed: A survey ship six months past its last relay contact. Small crew. The dark outside is very large.
Right, small label: WHAT CAME BACK
Right, in a serif reading face: Ito had stopped logging the silences. There were too many of them now, and writing them down had begun to feel like a way of counting. The relay had been dark for a hundred and eighty-one days. Outside the forward port there was nothing to look at, so the crew had mostly stopped looking.

SECTION TWO heading, small: AND THEN YOU HAVE TO DECIDE.

Story passage above the choices, serif: The door was not locked, which was the first thing wrong with it. Delacroix had gone in eleven minutes ago and had not come out. Somewhere below the floor a generator turned over, caught, and settled.

Three choice options, stacked, each a wide bordered block:
Option one: Go in after him.
Option two, marked as the one taken: Pick the lock on the side entrance instead.
Option three: Wait, and count the exits.

Small tag on the taken option: YOU CHOSE THIS

Below the choices, a small result marker: LOCKPICKING - FAILED
Consequence passage, serif, with its first sentence emphasised in the accent colour: The tension wrench turned a quarter and snapped. The sound was small and it was enough. Above, a chair scraped back, and the generator noise stopped being the loudest thing in the building. Delacroix knew someone was outside now, and so did whoever was with him.

Closing band, one line: Bring your own Google Gemini key. It takes about two minutes to set up, it stays in your browser, and there is no account to make.
Closing button, filled: Start your story
Closing text link: Get a Gemini key

Render every piece of the text above accurately and legibly, with correct spelling. Do not invent any additional text, prices, dates, statistics, ratings, testimonials, user counts, or company logos. Do not add any words from these instructions into the image.
